extracted.intended_audience: public speakers (Toastmasters members and others) seeking to write and deliver humorous material
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and delivering short jokes within speeches, focusing on structure (setup/punch), material selection, audience awareness, and delivery/timing. Emphasizes rules and a short evaluative rubric for use in spoken presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Part Structure (Setup and Punch line)
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup: furnishes information. Punch line: surprise twist on that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joke should be built as two parts: give the audience what they need to form expectations, then deliver a twist that reinterprets that information. Keep the relationship between setup and punch clear so the surprise lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter is created when surprise is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comedic surprise is "a twist without serious repercussions." (Echoes Benign Violation Theory.) Design the punch so it subverts expectations but doesn’t cause real harm; the twist should be unexpected yet coherent with the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misdirection
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience is led away from the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statements in the setup that encourage the audience to form the wrong interpretation; that misdirection makes the eventual punch more effective by increasing the surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth as Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Always begin with the truth. Identify assumptions in your opening statement. Explore alternative interpretations until you find a funny twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with truthful, relatable observations so the audience can recognize the premise; examine the assumptions and try different reinterpretations of the truth to discover the comic angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Give listeners all info needed to understand the punch. No unnecessary information that weakens the effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the joke as concise as possible—every word should contribute to building the setup or increasing the impact of the punch. Remove extraneous detail that diffuses the surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punch at the End
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the punch as close to the end as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t bury the punch in extra words or tags; structure the line so the twist arrives at the conclusion of the joke for maximum effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow Audience Reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't step on the audience's response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After delivering a punch, pause to allow time to laugh and soak in the humor. Avoid immediately talking over or rushing the reaction; good timing includes leaving space for audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAP — Material (truthful, relatable, specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material should be truthful, relatable, and specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose material grounded in truth that the audience can relate to; specificity helps listeners visualize and connects them emotionally to the premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAP — Audience (know who you're talking to)
rubrics_metrics.description: Know who you're talking to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor references, tone, and subject matter to the audience’s values, experiences, and sensibilities to increase relevance and avoid offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAP — Presentation (timing, delivery, eye contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation encompasses timing, delivery, and eye contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery mechanics—rhythm, pauses, vocal variation, and eye contact—shape how setup and punch are received. Practice presentation to control timing and maximize impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Make it relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure jokes connect to the speaker's topic or the audience’s experience so the humor feels natural and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Be original
rubrics_metrics.description: Be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clichés and predictable angles; originality increases surprise and audience enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Tell the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground jokes in honest observation rather than fabricated claims; plausibility helps the audience accept the setup and be surprised by the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Be self-deprecating (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be self-deprecating (when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-deprecation can defuse risk and build rapport, but use it judiciously and only when it fits the speaker and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Avoid offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid offensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of material that attacks or alienates audience members; offensive jokes undermine rapport and can derail a speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Rules of Humor — Practice your timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice your timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is a skill developed through rehearsal—work on pauses, pacing, and delivery to ensure the punch lands as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric — Is the setup truthful and relatable?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the setup truthful and relatable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the opening premise is based in truth and will connect with the audience’s experience; linked to MAP Material and 'Tell the truth' rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric — Is there clear misdirection toward the wrong interpretation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there clear misdirection toward the wrong interpretation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the setup intentionally steers the audience toward an incorrect assumption that the punch can overturn to produce surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric — Is the punch as close to the end as possible?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the punch as close to the end as possible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the punch arrives at the conclusion of the joke rather than being preceded or followed by unnecessary material that weakens impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric — Is every word necessary (concision)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is every word necessary (concision)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the joke contains only the words essential to building the setup and delivering the punch; remove anything that dilutes the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric — Does the speaker allow audience reaction?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the speaker allow audience reaction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether the performer pauses and permits laughter rather than talking over or prematurely moving on, preserving timing and audience engagement.
